subject: How to keep a dashboard app running for long periods

messages.author: 1d22b88696fb889c
messages.subject: How to keep a dashboard app running for long periods
parts:
I've created a Shiny dashboard app that I want to run, without user interaction, for many hours a day. However, the instance inactivity timer kicks in and shuts it down. It appears that the max inactivity time allowed is 60 minutes. What technique should be used to allow a dashboard app to run for long periods?

Thanks,
Eric

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: How to keep a dashboard app running for long periods
parts:
Eric,

Please try setting the following:

Settings -> Advanced -> Connection Timeout

Fereshteh

messages.subject: Re: How to keep a dashboard app running for long periods
parts:
Back in the early days of shiny my trick was to have a reactive that updated every few seconds, with a quasi hidden nondescript output tied to it.

Bootleg, but it really worked like a charm.

messages.author: e84e7628b5f8a3e1
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Re: How to keep a dashboard app running for long periods
parts:
Eric,

If your dashboard is only doing server to client updates then you need to set "Read Timeout" to something higher like 8 hours.

-ANdy
On Thu, Feb 18, 2016 at 10:37 AM, Eric Goldsmith <er...@goldsmithgroup.org> wrote:
